transcript.text:
Sorry to hear that. To narrow it down, it helps to know what type of hob you have and what exactly it's doing. Here are the most common problems and fixes for each type:

## ⚠️ Safety first
• Smell gas? Turn off the hob and the gas supply at the meter, don't use switches or flames, open windows, leave the property, and call the gas emergency line (in the UK: 0800 111 999).
• Burning smell, sparking, or tripping the electrics? Switch it off at the isolator switch or fuse box and don't use it until it's checked.

## 🔥 Gas hob
| Problem | Likely cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Clicks but won't light | Burner cap misaligned, or burner/igniter dirty or wet. Clean, dry thoroughly, and reseat the cap. |
| Lights but goes out when you let go of the knob | Thermocouple (the small metal probe by the flame) is dirty or faulty. Hold the knob in for 10–15 seconds. Clean the probe gently. If that doesn't work it may need replacing. |
| Weak, uneven, or yellow flame | Blocked burner holes. Clean with a pin or soft brush. |
| No clicking at all | Check the hob's plug or fuse. The igniter may be faulty. |

## ⚡ Electric / ceramic hob
| Problem | Likely cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Whole hob dead | Check the fuse box or circuit breaker and the cooker isolator switch. |
| One ring not heating | Faulty element or energy regulator (control switch). This usually needs an engineer. |
| Ring stuck on high | Faulty energy regulator. |
| Cracked glass | Stop using it immediately and get it replaced. |

## 🧲 Induction hob
| Problem | Likely cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Won't turn on / beeps | Child lock may be on. Usually you hold the key/lock symbol for a few seconds. |
| Zone flashes, won't heat | Pan isn't induction-compatible (test: a magnet should stick to the base), or the pan is too small for the zone. |
| Error code (e.g. E, F, U + number) | Look it up in the manual. Try switching off at the isolator for 5–10 minutes to reset. |
| Controls not responding | Wipe the touch panel dry. Water or spills interfere with it. |
| Cuts out during cooking | Overheating. Check the fan vents underneath aren't blocked. |

---

Tell me:
1. Gas, electric ceramic, or induction?
2. Brand/model (if known)?
3. What's happening: not turning on, not heating, error code, one ring only, etc.?

With that I can give you more specific steps.
It's an electric ceramic hob, a Zanussi. The rear right ring isn't heating up, the other three are fine.

Since the other three rings work, the power supply is fine and the fault is almost certainly with that one ring. On a ceramic hob it's usually one of three things.

## Quick checks first
1. Does the control respond for that ring? Does the display show a number, or does the knob click and turn as normal?
2. Does the ring glow at all, even faintly, after a few minutes on high?
3. Is it a dual or extended zone? On some Zanussi models the rear ring has an extra button or a knob position for an outer circuit. Check that only part of it isn't working.
4. Reset it. Switch the hob off at the cooker isolator switch (the big red switch on the wall) for about 10 minutes, then try again. This sometimes clears a glitch on touch-control models.

## Likely causes
| Symptom | Most likely cause |
|---|---|
| Control works normally, but the ring never glows | Failed heating element (most common) or a burnt wire or connector to it |
| Ring glows but switches off quickly or heats weakly | Faulty thermal limiter (part of the element) or the element is failing |
| Ring stuck on full, or no control at all over that ring | Energy regulator (knob models) or control board/relay (touch models) |
| Display shows an error code | Look up the code in your manual or on Zanussi's website |

## Can you fix it yourself?
If you're comfortable with electrics, you can test the element:
• Turn off the power at the fuse box/consumer unit, not just the isolator.
• Lift the hob out and check the element's terminals with a multimeter on resistance (Ω).
• A working element typically reads about 20–50 Ω, depending on its wattage. A reading of open circuit (OL / infinite) means it's dead.
• Also look for scorched or loose wires at the terminals and at the control.

If you're not confident, get an engineer. These hobs are often hard-wired on a high-current circuit.

## Getting the right part / repair
• Find the model number and PNC on the rating plate. It's usually on the underside of the hob, and sometimes on a sticker in the manual or on the original box.
• Replacement elements usually cost around £30–£70. An engineer's repair is typically £80–£150 in total, including parts.
• Check your warranty. Zanussi (Electrolux) hobs are often covered for 1–2 years, and some retailers offer longer. If it's under warranty, book a repair through Zanussi rather than opening it up.

If you tell me whether it has knobs or touch controls, and whether the ring glows at all, I can narrow it down further.

It's touch controls, and the number shows up fine for that ring. It doesn't glow at all though. I'm not sure if it's a dual zone one. The manual says ZHRN on the cover but I don't know the rest of the model number.

That pattern (touch control responds and shows a power level, but the ring never glows) points strongly to a failed heating element. That's the most common fault on ceramic hobs. The control is sending power, but it isn't getting through the element.

## Is it a dual zone?
Check these:
• On the glass: a dual zone has two circles printed around that ring, one inside the other.
• On the touch panel: look for a button or symbol showing a small circle inside a larger one, near that ring's controls.

If it is dual zone and neither part glows, it's still most likely the element.

## One more useful test
Turn the ring on and listen closely. You should hear a faint click from the control board as a relay switches on (and repeated clicks as it cycles).
• Click, but no glow: almost certainly the element, its built-in thermal limiter, or a burnt wire or connector to it.
• No click at all: possibly a faulty relay on the control board, which is a less common and more expensive fix.

Compare with one of the working rings so you know what the click sounds like.

## Finding the full model number
ZHRN is just the start (Zanussi ceramic hob range). You'll want the full model number plus the PNC (a 9-digit product number) to order the correct part. Try:
• Underneath the hob: the rating plate is on the base. If there's a drawer or cupboard below (not an oven), you can sometimes see it by removing the drawer and looking up. Take a phone photo.
• Paperwork: the guarantee card, receipt, or a sticker inside or on the back of the manual.
• Original box or installation sheet, if you still have them.

If an oven sits underneath, the hob may need lifting out to read the plate. Turn the power off at the consumer unit first.

## Repair or replace?
• A replacement element is usually a fairly affordable part. With an engineer's call-out and labour, the total is typically a mid-range repair bill.
• If the hob is old, it's worth getting a quote and comparing it with the price of a new basic ceramic hob before going ahead.

In the meantime, it's fine to keep using the other three rings, as long as there's no burning smell, cracked glass, or tripping electrics.

If you find the full model number, let me know and I can help you work out what to look for when ordering the part.

I'm not sure I can tell the click, to be honest. Do you mean I should just turn it on and listen? I'll have a go. I did smell something slightly burnt from that ring once a couple of weeks ago, but not since.

Yes, just turn it on and listen. It's optional, so don't worry if you can't hear anything.

## How to do the click test
1. Make the kitchen as quiet as possible (extractor fan, radio, and dishwasher off).
2. Turn on a working ring first, set it to a high number, and put your ear close to the glass near the controls. You're listening for a soft "tick" just after you press the button.
3. Do the same with the faulty ring and compare.

If you can't hear a click on either ring, that's fine. Some relays are very quiet. An engineer can test it properly in a minute or two with a meter.

## About the burnt smell
This is a useful clue. It fits with the element or its wiring failing:
• An element often burns out at the end of its life, which can give off a brief smell before it stops working.
• It can also mean a wire or connector to that ring overheated and burnt through, which would also stop it heating.
• It could just have been a spill burning off, but given the ring failed around the same time, the element or wiring is more likely.

## What to do in the meantime
• Leave that ring switched off and don't keep testing it repeatedly.
• Using the other three rings is generally fine.
• If you smell burning again, see smoke, or the hob trips the electrics, switch off at the cooker isolator and stop using the hob until it's checked. An overheated connection can get worse and affect the wiring.
• When you book an engineer, mention the burnt smell. It helps them check the wiring and terminals as well as the element.

If you can get the full model number and PNC from the rating plate, I can help you work out what to ask for or roughly what the part should cost.
